question: What post-subagent completion contract, if any, should OpenClaw expose for plugins, and should it allow observation only, announcement mutation/suppression, delivery-status visibility, or a broader generic delivery boundary?
rationale: The missing source surface is clear, but the payload, child-history access, plugin authority, timeout/error behavior, delivery audit trail, and relationship to the rejected guard-hook PR are public API and security choices that automation should not lock in.

options.title: Generic Typed Delivery Boundary
options.body: Define one bounded hook or lifecycle contract for completion metadata and delivery decisions, avoiding the rejected PR's subagent-only guard-hook shape while preserving explicit security and audit semantics.

options.title: Observation-Only Completion Event
options.body: Expose a non-mutating subagent completion event for metrics, trajectories, and indexing, while leaving suppression or routing to separate delivery-policy work.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Lifecycle Hooks
options.body: Keep this issue open but defer implementation until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43454 settles a unified lifecycle hook model across subagents, turns, and thresholds.

recommendation.title: Generic Typed Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Define one bounded hook or lifecycle contract for completion metadata and delivery decisions, avoiding the rejected PR's subagent-only guard-hook shape while preserving explicit security and audit semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest maintainer review on the overlapping guard-hook PR provides the strongest current product/security direction for this boundary.
